text.p: Belgian investment magazine Cash! said on Thursday shares in Belgian telecommunications company Telinfo were now a 'sell'.
"Reap the handsome profits and sell the stock," Cash! said. It based its recommendation on a share price of 1,930 francs. Telinfo closed at 1,910 francs on Wednesday.

Telinfo shares have gained 49 percent since the start of the year. Cash! said mainly Anglo-Saxon investors drove up the share because of Telinfo's 10 percent stake in Belgium's second GSM operator Mobistar whose performance has been largely exceeding expectations.
Cash! recommended buying shares in holding company Mosane for those who wanted to invest in Mobistar. Mosane has a five percent Mobistar stake.

It said that based on the current price, Telinfo would still have an extremely high price/earnings ratio of 34 and 26 for 1997 and 1998 on the basis of the current price, even if the profit rose 30 percent per year in the next two years.
It said this gave a fair valuation of 1,680 francs per share on the basis of a 30 percent annual profit growth in the next three years.
"So Telinfo's bright prospects are being paid for very expensively. The current price reflects Telinfo's profit potential to an exaggerated extent," Cash! said.
